name: Fatima Olsen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What is a regular day like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and have managed the group-booking desk of a large hotel company for eight years. Five coordinators report to me. We reserve rooms for conferences, check deposit dates and call event organisers when the ballroom layout changes. I have a bachelor’s degree, and I know the usual contract problems, though a complicated cancellation still goes to our legal team. I sometimes use an approved AI tool to draft a plain confirmation, then check every room count.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What keeps you busy at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband runs a small tailoring shop, and our children are nine and fourteen. We have a mortgage and about three months of household expenses saved. My pay is typical for this role, and there are some other hotel-management jobs nearby. I like reliable work and teaching a new coordinator how to ask a customer one clear question before promising a room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the booking team AI Plateau is a little help with confirmations. A hotel still has to have the promised rooms and chairs when a group walks in.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think our desk stays and my pay holds. The tailoring shop can be quiet between busy seasons, so three months saved gives me comfort but not a reason to ignore the mortgage. A small AI change is less worrying than a cancelled event.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the weekly room-block check with each hotel and use the approved AI tool only for first drafts. If a minor new feature appears, I’d test it on last season’s changed bookings before sending any live confirmation. We would keep our regular savings transfer in months when both incomes arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the shop’s slow months, but my hotel job looks safe. A faster confirmation would not change our household plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What changed in a booking last season?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A conference asked for eighty chairs, then changed to round tables that seated fewer people. The hotel confirmation promised eighty seats, but round tables left room for only sixty. I called the organiser before the event and we changed the room plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you do when the shop is slow?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We pay the fixed bills from my salary and use a little of the reserve for materials if needed. We refill it after a busy month. I would not borrow for a bigger shop just because one month went well.

say: **AI Plateau** may speed confirmations, but the hotel must supply real rooms and seats.
I’d keep the **weekly room check** with each property.
think: My hotel **job and pay** look safe under a small tool change.
The tailoring shop’s **slow months** still matter to our mortgage.
do: **Keep** weekly checks of hotel room blocks in 2026.
**Test** the new feature on changed bookings before live confirmation.
**Continue** regular savings transfers when both incomes arrive.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about the shop’s slow months while hotel work stays secure.
S0.quote: The hotel confirmation promised eighty seats, but round tables left room for only sixty.
fieldNote: Her **three-month reserve** covers brief shop slumps but does not erase mortgage attention.
She catches a **room-layout error** by speaking to the organiser before arrival.

steps.text: Check hotel room blocks weekly before confirming group bookings
Test new confirmation feature on changed bookings from last season
Continue savings transfers only in months when both incomes arrive

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption can draft offers, book rooms, check deposits and answer common event questions. The company should measure failed promises as well as booking speed before it cuts staff.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Most of my desk tasks are on that list. I am experienced at calming an organiser, but the company could join two booking desks and need one manager rather than two. Three months saved helps us look for another job, though the shop income is not steady enough to replace my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This quarter I’d compare AI-generated room plans with ten events whose layouts changed late, and show any wrong seat counts to my director. I’d take paid training on the approved system if the hotel offers a place. If booking posts shrink, I’d apply for a nearby event-operations lead role only after checking its pay, weekend rota and school pickup with my husband.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a possible manager cut. I can test the tool, but I cannot count a future event job as mine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which mistake costs money?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If an organiser asks for round tables and we promise eighty seats in a room that holds sixty, we may need a second room. The extra staff and furniture cost more than the saved minutes on a confirmation. I would show that cost.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the weekend rota?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My husband’s shop is busiest on Saturdays, and our nine-year-old cannot be left alone all day. An event job might mean every Saturday. We would need an actual rota before I applied.

say: I’d say **Steady Disruption** could automate offers, bookings, deposits and routine event questions.
I would measure **failed seat promises** alongside booking speed before any staff cuts.
think: A merged booking desk could remove **one manager post**, possibly mine.
Our **three-month reserve** buys a search, but shop income cannot replace my wage.
do: **Compare** AI room plans with ten changed-layout events this quarter.
**Take** paid system training if the hotel offers a place.
**Apply** for event operations only if pay, weekend rota and child pickup work.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible cut to my manager role.
S1.quote: The extra staff and furniture cost more than the saved minutes on a confirmation.
fieldNote: She compares **event costs** with software speed rather than trusting a booking count.
A new job needs **Saturday care** because the tailoring shop is busiest then.

steps.text: Compare ten changed event layouts with AI room plans and costs
Take paid booking-system training only if hotel offers a place
Apply for event-operations vacancy only if pay weekend rota and child pickup work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could write group contracts, plan rooms and answer organisers without most of our desk. We should ask for a cut date and a named hotel worker who owns a bad booking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full thinking AI by 2028 could do much of my screen work. Robots able to set rooms and move furniture arrive around 2031, but the operations lead’s schedules and reports would face AGI in 2028 too. I expect the desk to contract and might lose my manager post. Our three-month reserve and nearby hotels give me some control.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I’d ask the regional director for written dates and severance figures, then talk to my husband about Saturdays and the mortgage. In 2027 I’d apply for two posted event-operations roles only if pay after travel covers our house and the rota lets an adult care for our younger child. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I’m cut, I’d take a confirmed operations offer; otherwise I’d use the reserve for bills while searching.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. I do not expect to be without options, but a lost salary would end our plan to repair the shop this year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell them I may work at a hotel instead of the booking office, but we are not moving on a guess. The older child could get home alone; the younger still needs an adult. My husband and I would plan from a real rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is the shop repair?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The cutting table needs replacing, and we have been saving for it. We would delay that purchase if my hotel pay stopped. I would not spend our mortgage reserve on a new cutting table for my husband’s tailoring shop.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs cut dates and a named person for bad bookings.
I would ask for **severance figures** before changing jobs.
think: Booking and operations planning face **2028 AGI**, before room-setting robots around 2031.
My post might go, but **three months saved** and nearby hotels give options.
do: **Apply** for two posted event jobs only if pay after travel covers mortgage and childcare rota works.
**Accept** a confirmed operations offer after 2028 only if those pay and care conditions still hold.
**Delay** buying the shop cutting table if hotel salary stops.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible lost salary and delayed shop repair.
S2.quote: I would not spend our mortgage reserve on a new cutting table for my husband’s tailoring shop.
fieldNote: She expects a **smaller desk**, but treats her own job loss as possible, with local alternatives.
The **cutting-table delay** is a specific family-business spending choice if her wage stops.

steps.text: Apply for posted event roles only if pay after travel covers mortgage and childcare rota works
Accept confirmed event offer after 2028 only if travel-adjusted pay covers mortgage and childcare works
Delay buying shop cutting table if hotel salary stops

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives five years to find out whether a person still has to settle event trouble on site. I would want a paid assignment that tests that work, not a certificate alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My group-booking desk could go in 2031, and event operations still has planning and reports exposed then. Robots that set up rooms arrive around 2034, so the hands-on part changes later. Five years lets me try a property role while I still have wages, but no vacancy is promised.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From early 2027 I’d take two paid event shifts with an operations lead if the director covers my booking desk and keeps my salary. I’d learn how room changes are handled when guests are already arriving. After 2031 I’d apply for an operations lead vacancy only if it still includes real event work, pays our mortgage after travel and has a rota our family can cover.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but two real shifts would answer more than another screen course. I would not leave the booking team short to prove a point.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do on the shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Watch the organiser arrive, count the seats and help move the room plan when the number is wrong. I know the hotel contract, not the rhythm of setting a conference room. I would ask the lead to tell me where I slow things down.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your director refuses desk cover?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would offer to take one paid shift in a quieter week, not unpaid leave. My coordinators still need a manager for deposit questions. The trial is only useful if both desks can operate.

say: **Five years** allows a paid event-shift trial before changing roles.
I would test **real room changes**, not collect a certificate.
think: Booking and operations paperwork face **2031 AGI**, before room robots around 2034.
An operations **vacancy** may not be open when I need it.
do: **Take** two paid event shifts in 2027 only with booking cover and full salary.
**Learn** live room changes from the operations lead during those shifts.
**Apply** after 2031 only if real event work, net mortgage pay and family rota fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the desk, with time to test on-site work.
S3.quote: I know the hotel contract, not the rhythm of setting a conference room.
fieldNote: She tests a **two-shift assignment** rather than assuming booking skill qualifies her for event operations.
The **trial and later job** both require protected pay and workable family hours.

steps.text: Take two paid event shifts only with booking-desk cover and full salary
Learn live room changes from operations lead during paid shifts
Apply after 2031 only for event post with live work, net mortgage pay and family rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to see which hotel jobs still have guests and staff in front of them. The company should publish vacancies and wages rather than say everyone can retrain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 our children will be about nineteen and twenty-four. If both incomes hold, we could pay down more mortgage and add to savings. My booking work and the planning part of event operations face AGI in 2036, while room-setting robots follow around 2039. I would not call any job permanent, but the time helps.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the room-block check and add a little to savings only after the mortgage and shop bills clear. I’d review event-operations postings each year with my husband. Before 2036 I’d take a paid hotel assignment only if the salary and rota suit us; after AGI arrives I’d stay only while the role includes real guest work and pays our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about what remains in a decade. I can plan, but today’s mortgage is still due on its usual date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much would you add to savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe forty after a busy shop month and both paychecks arrive. I would check the shop’s rent and our mortgage first. If either is short, we would skip the transfer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you expand the shop instead?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not before we replace the cutting table and see a full year of orders. My husband knows his customers, but he would not take on a second lease from one busy season. We would need a full year of tailoring orders before leasing a second shop.

say: A **decade** should bring posted hotel vacancies with real wages and duties before workers choose a course.
I would choose **guest-facing work** that still pays our household bills after the booking desk changes.
think: Two incomes could reduce the **mortgage** and grow savings if they hold.
Booking and operations planning face **2036 AGI**, before room robots around 2039.
do: **Save** forty only after a busy shop month, both paychecks, shop rent and home mortgage clear.
**Take** a paid event role only with suitable salary and rota; stay after 2036 only with guest work and bill-covering pay.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about future hotel work while current bills continue.
S4.quote: We would need a full year of tailoring orders before leasing a second shop.
fieldNote: Her **savings plan** waits for a busy shop month, both paychecks, shop rent and the home mortgage.
She wants **guest-facing work** but admits its planning tasks remain exposed to thinking AI.

steps.text: Keep checking hotel room blocks before group confirmations
Save forty only after busy shop month, both wages, shop rent and mortgage clear
Take paid event role only if salary and family rota fit and guest work remains
Stay in event role after 2036 only with guest work and bill-covering pay

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the booking desk could shrink before I have done enough event work to be hired elsewhere. A cut date, actual severance and paid shifts on site would help me decide. Three months saved buys a little time, not a guaranteed hotel job.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the organiser standing in a room with sixty chairs after ordering eighty. A confirmation email cannot add twenty seats. Someone has to find another room before the guests arrive.

headlineQuote: A confirmation email cannot add twenty seats.
portrait: **Fatima, 43**, has eight years managing group bookings at a large hotel company and holds a bachelor’s degree.
Her **typical pay**, tailoring-shop husband, three-month reserve and some nearby hotels support a mortgage and two school-age children.
She uses **AI occasionally** but checks real room layouts and deposit promises with hotel staff.
She is **uneasy** under AI Plateau, anxious about faster desk cuts and tests event work only with protected wages and family hours.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink her booking desk before she gains enough live event experience.
whatWouldHelp: A firm **cut date**, numeric severance and paid site shifts would help her decide.
